newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan trade surplus rising trend unchanged--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan trade surplus rising trend unchanged--MOF.

text.p: A trend that started in April for Japan's trade surplus to rise has not changed at present, a Ministry of Finance (MOF) source told Reuters on Wednesday.
A rise in Japan's trade surplus for the first 20 days of July was mainly due to double-digit growth in car exports, the official said.

The ministry announced earlier that Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus rose 126.4 percent to 480.57 billion yen in the first 20 days of July compared with a revised surplus of 212.26 billion yen in the same period a year ago.
"There is no change in the the general trend (of the rise) in the surplus," he said, adding that he could not predict whether the surplus would continue to grow or not.

Ministry data showed exports rising 10.5 percent to 2.64 trillion yen from a year earlier in the first 20 days of July. The growth was mainly from car exports, though computer and office equipment shipments also played a part, he said.
The yen weakened against the dollar some four percent in the first 20 days of July compared to the same period last year, he said.
Meanwhile, imports fell 0.8 percent from a year earlier to 2.15 trillion yen in the 20-day period. Although imports of meat and crude oil showed steady growth, a rise in car imports slowed, he said.

Compared with other such periods, it was the first time since August 1995 that imports had shown negative growth in the first 20 days of any month. In the first 20 days of August 1995, imports fell 4.6 percent from a year earlier, he said.
